title: Inbound campaigns
blurb: DNIS, run state, scripts, overflow, schedules, and the pause between calls.
summary: Inbound is a running campaign plus a script. Busy means the campaign is not in the call.

lessons.title: A DNIS answers only while the campaign runs
objectives: Tie DNIS, run state, and IVR together
paragraphs: An inbound campaign receives calls for a DNIS and processes them with that campaign's IVR script. The inbound topic is blunt about state: if the campaign is not running, callers hear a busy signal.
Greetings, skills, and hold music never get a chance to run in that state. The first check on a new number is the campaign state, not the carrier.

lessons.title: The script is the inbound product
objectives: Remember that connect ends the script
paragraphs: Once the campaign answers, the IVR script is the product the caller meets. The inbound topic lists custom greetings, loops and branching, collecting information, using contact data, voicemail when the queue is long, forward to a third party, and priority.

Skill Transfer is how that script hands the caller to a queue. The community article says that after an agent is connected, the IVR script is complete. A module after Skill Transfer is not a second conversation with the same caller.
uncertain: A post-call survey exists as a campaign-admin topic title in the docs tree. This lesson does not describe its screens. Open that topic before you design one.

lessons.title: Queue treatment is a choice, not a hope
objectives: Do not use a stopped campaign as a prompt
paragraphs: The inbound topic allows custom prompts and hold music, a message when agents are unavailable, voicemail, and a forward to a third party. Those are different exits. Hold music is not voicemail. A forward leaves your agents entirely.
Third Party Transfer is an IVR module in the modules list. Voicemail Transfer is another. Picking the wrong one is a routing bug, not a carrier bug.

lessons.title: Priority and service level
objectives: Point at the screen for each
paragraphs: The inbound topic says you can prioritize inbound traffic. Skill Transfer has a Priority tab in the community write-up. Skill groups themselves have service-level settings in the basic admin topic.

Priority is not the same number as a service-level target. One decides who gets the next agent when several calls wait. The other is how you measure whether the wait was acceptable. The public pages name both. They do not, in the text this lab read, give you a formula that mixes them.
uncertain: The exact numeric interaction between skill service level and Skill Transfer priority is not stated in the pages this lab quoted.

lessons.title: Schedules, not a stopped campaign
objectives: Prefer a schedule to a stopped campaign
paragraphs: The campaign admin tree includes IVR script schedules for autodial and inbound campaigns. The planning topic tells you to set the campaign IVR schedule after the script exists. A schedule swaps treatment by time. Stopping the campaign does not. Stopping it returns busy.
This lab does not reproduce the schedule dialog field by field. Use the schedule when you need a night path, and confirm the campaign stays running.

lessons.title: Pause before the next call
objectives: Do not expect it in the hold column
paragraphs: Skill Transfer has Pause Before Transfer, in seconds, on the General tab. The default is 0. A value above 0 waits that long after an agent is selected before the call is delivered, so a queue does not slap the next call down instantly.

The community article says those seconds do not show as On Hold in a report. On Plus applications the caller can sit in a Connecting state. Setting the pause to 0 removes that connecting bar. Do not 'fix' a report by deleting the pause if agents asked for the breath.

fault.fix: Set a few seconds of pause and give them a real disposition timer if they need wrap.

lessons.title: Inbound design review
objectives: Escalate to the trunk only after they pass
paragraphs: A review you can finish in one sitting: DNIS, running campaign, script, skill on the Outbound Skills tab, overflow module, schedule, and pause. Each one has a public page. None of them is a trunk setting.
If all seven are right and the caller still hears silence or reorder, then you have a carrier or SBC symptom. The topology bench is the next tool, not another copy of the greeting.
